project.title: D3.js / Data-Driven Documents
project.subtitle: Data as Interface
project.format: Open-source JavaScript library; academic research paper; web visualization framework
intendedAudience: people making custom web-based data graphics
project.oneSentence: D3.js is an open-source JavaScript library and design method for creating custom, interactive, data-driven graphics in the browser by binding data directly to web document elements.
project.workingThesis: D3 changed web visualization by making data directly drive browser documents, turning the webpage into a programmable visual system rather than a static display or a fixed chart template.

sections.whyPrecedent: D3 is a computational design precedent because it changes how visual form is produced. The designer writes relationships between data, document elements, scales, shapes, interaction, and time. The final graphic is not drawn once by hand; it is generated, updated, and transformed through code.
historicalContext: Before D3, many web visualization tools hid the rendered graphic inside toolkit-specific abstractions. D3's original paper framed its approach as representation-transparent: instead of hiding the scenegraph, D3 lets designers inspect and manipulate the browser's native DOM.

D3 followed Protovis, an earlier JavaScript visualization toolkit associated with the Stanford Visualization Group. D3 moved away from an intermediate representation layer and toward direct manipulation of standard web documents, making custom visualization more flexible, inspectable, and compatible with ordinary web development tools.
sections.visualLogic: D3 does not impose one visual style. Its visual language is modular and procedural: charts, maps, networks, diagrams, dashboards, and narrative graphics are composed from primitives. Its aesthetic significance is flexibility: visual form can be custom-built for the dataset, often with animation, interaction, annotation, and responsive layout.
sections.communityOfPractice: D3 became important through an open-source ecosystem, not only through a single publication. Its community includes academic visualization researchers, web developers, designers, data journalists, Observable notebook users, GitHub contributors, tutorial writers, and practitioners who publish examples and reusable code.
sections.preliminaryAssessment: D3 gives designers direct control over how data becomes visual form in the browser. It helped bring interactive data visualization into mainstream web practice and influenced journalism, civic technology, research, and creative coding. Its weakness is the same as its strength: because it is low-level and flexible, it can be difficult for beginners and can privilege people who already understand code.

methods.name: Data binding
methods.does: Connects arrays or structured data to selected DOM elements.
methods.matters: Makes data the driver of visual form.

methods.name: Data join
methods.does: Defines enter, update, and exit states between data and visual elements.

methods.name: Selections
methods.does: Selects document elements and applies transformations.
methods.matters: Gives designers direct control over HTML and SVG elements.

methods.name: Scales
methods.does: Maps data values to visual values such as position, size, and color.
methods.matters: Converts abstract data into readable visual encodings.

methods.name: Axes
methods.does: Displays scale reference marks and labels.

methods.name: Shapes
methods.does: Generates SVG paths for lines, areas, arcs, symbols, and links.

methods.name: Interaction modules
methods.does: Supports brushing, dragging, zooming, filtering, and hover states.
methods.matters: Makes visualization exploratory rather than static.

methods.name: Web standards
methods.does: Uses HTML, SVG, CSS, Canvas, JavaScript, and the DOM.
methods.matters: Makes the browser the design medium.

criticalQuestions: Who gains visual power when data visualization becomes programmable?
Who is excluded when expressive visualization requires JavaScript, browser knowledge, and data-structure knowledge?
Does D3 democratize visualization, or does it mainly empower people who already know how to code?
How does D3 change the relationship between designer, data, document, and audience?

sourceNotes.interpretation: The official D3 site says D3 was created by Mike Bostock in 2011 and that the D3 paper was co-authored with Jeffrey Heer and Vadim Ogievetsky. Information is Beautiful credits D3 to Mike Bostock, Jason Davies, and Philippe Riviere. This study keeps these categories separate: creator, paper authors, and major contributors.
2011 is used as the project and paper year. Several important explanatory essays were published in 2012.
The format is intentionally broad: open-source JavaScript library, research paper, and web visualization framework.
Audience is inferred from official descriptions, documented use cases, source-code community, and reception in visualization practice.
